# Data and Background

For this part, we are going to reference Jeremy Balka's (Simple Linear Regression example)[https://www.jbstatistics.com/simple-linear-regression-an-example/] that uses data from Anapaca Island pelicans. It explores how DDT levels affect the thickness of the bird's eggs.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
anacapa$locality <- "Anacapa"
anacapa <- anacapa[c("locality", "sample_no", "thickness_mm",
                       "DDE", "total_DDT", "PCB")]
```

By using this example, we can compare his intercept and covariate coefficient (for DDT) to the our bayesian found ones.

```{r simple_plot}

plot(anacapa$total_DDT, anacapa$thickness_mm, xlab="DDT (ppm)",
     ylab ="Shell Thickness (mm)", main="DDT Affect on Shell Thickness")

# 1. Fit a linear model
model <- lm(thickness_mm ~ total_DDT, data = anacapa)

# 2. Extract residuals
res <- resid(model)

# 3. Plot basic histogram
hist(res, 
     main = "Histogram of Residuals", 
     xlab = "Residuals", 
     col = "lightblue", 
     border = "black")

```
